description: errorMessage is nonstandard — Ajv gets it from the ajv-errors plugin, and jsonschema-validate implements the same portable subset independently by reading the messages out of the schema JSON. Two independent implementations of one behavior is exactly the shape that wants a conformance suite, and an authored message is the one place the two legs are contracted to emit the identical sentence.

cases.name: a relative pointer crashes ajv-validate when the failing keyword is type
cases.description: ${0} is meant to be the failing value itself, wherever it occurs. It works wherever some other keyword forces Ajv to bind that value to a variable.

items.errorMessage: each artifact must be a string; ${0} is not

jsonschema-validate: INVALID: /1: each artifact must be a string; 7 is not

defect.summary: ajv-validate crashes. A relative pointer in a subschema whose failing keyword is `type` makes ajv-errors emit JSON.stringify(dataN) for a variable Ajv's codegen never bound, and the generated validator throws ReferenceError. The crash exits 1 — the INVALID code — with nothing on stdout, so a caller scripting on exit status reads a crash as a verdict.
defect.should: The wrapper should catch anything thrown during validation and exit 2, since a crash is a fact about the setup and not about the instance. The underlying ajv-errors incompatibility should be reported upstream; adding any keyword that forces Ajv to bind the value (pattern, for one) is the current workaround.

cases.description: ${1/digest} climbs one level from the failing value and descends again.

cases.name: an unresolvable pointer is left as written by one leg and replaced with undefined by the other
cases.description: A pointer that does not resolve is left in the message verbatim rather than guessed at.

defect.summary: The two errorMessage implementations disagree on an unresolvable pointer: jsonschema-validate leaves ${/nonexistent/path} in the message as written, and ajv-errors substitutes the text `undefined`.
defect.should: The portable subset must pick one behavior and both legs must implement it. Leaving the pointer as written is the honest one — `undefined` asserts a value the instance does not have.
